findings.description: AWS access key and secret access key are hard-coded in plaintext in the EC2 user_data script, which is stored in the instance metadata and Terraform state, exposing long-lived credentials to anyone with access to the instance or state file.
The security group allows inbound TCP port 22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing administrative access to the entire internet.

The security group allows inbound TCP port 80 from 0.0.0.0/0. Combined with the public subnet and public IP assignment, this exposes the web service to unrestricted access with no compensating controls (e.g., WAF, TLS).
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IP addresses to instances launched in this subnet, increasing the attack surface.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IP addresses to instances launched in this subnet, increasing the attack surface.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true or specify a KMS key, so data stored on the volume is unencrypted at rest.
The EBS snapshot inherits the lack of encryption from the source volume, leaving backup data unencrypted at rest.

The S3 bucket used to store VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration (e.g., aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration), leaving potentially sensitive network log data unencrypted at rest.

findings.issue_category: missing access controls / public access block
findings.description: The S3 bucket has no bucket policy, ACL restriction, or public access block configuration defined, and force_destroy is enabled, risking accidental public exposure or data loss of flow log data.
